messages:
maya: quick FYI — rerank embeddings in prod-us-east showing a sudden p95 token latency jump around 02:15 UTC. looked tied to a kernel rollout on accel-3.

samir: saw the alert. p95 up from ~29ms -> ~68ms for /rerank, QPS steady ~430. any kernel notes?

maya: rollout id 0x8b2c applied int4-merge attention kernel to 35% of accel-3 at 2026-01-08T02:14:00Z.

perf-bot: rollout 0x8b2c: int4-merge applied to accel-3 (35%) at 02:14 UTC — automated perf check triggered.

julie: did anything else change (KV/cache configs, routing)?

maya: KV hit-rate dropped ~0.90 -> 0.70 in same minute. avg tokens-per-batch increased.

liam: that KV drop will change runtime profile a lot. do we have kernel-launch counts by route?

samir: not per-route today. snapshot metrics around the window:
- route: /rerank
- QPS: 430 -> 425
- avg tokens/batch: 2.8 -> 5.6
- avg requests/batch: 1.2 -> 2.4
- kv_hit_rate: 0.90 -> 0.70
- embed_dim: 1024

julie: int4-merge is higher throughput for big mats but has nontrivial per-launch overhead that shows up with many small runs. KV misses produce more short-loop runs.

maya: grabbed a sample trace id trace_20260108_0216_4410 and generated a GPU flame snippet:
```
GPU timeline (sample trace_20260108_0216_4410):
- attention/int4-merge   50%\n- kv-serialize           18%\n- softmax/rng            9%\n- device-memcopy         13%\n- small-kernel-launch    10% (120us avg)
``` 

samir: timeline confirms frequent small kernel launches with memcpy between. Datadog span shows kernel-launch overhead ~110-140us on accel-3 with int4-merge.

liam: hypothesis: kernel selector chose int4-merge based on historic seq-length distribution. rerank route becomes bimodal when cache misses spike, causing more short runs and launch overhead amplification.

maya: instrumentation gaps: we have token-level latency breakdown, but we don't emit per-route kernel_launch_count or per-route memcpy_us. would be helpful to correlate.

perf-bot: suggested metric queries:
- sum:runtime.kernel_launch_count{route:rerank,env:prod}.rollup(sum,60)
- avg:runtime.memcpy_us{route:rerank,env:prod}.rollup(avg,60)
- histogram:runtime.req_batch_size{by:route,tag:kv_hit} (proposed)

samir: also want a derived alert: if kernel_launch_count / token_count > X for a route or if avg memcpy_us spikes > threshold.

julie: repro on staging: forced KV misses + int4-merge reproduces p95 ~70ms. swapping to int8-fused drops p95 back to ~30ms.

liam: short-term plan:
1) rollback int4-merge canary on accel-3 for rerank (35% -> 0%)
2) add per-route kernel_launch_count and memcpy_us metrics, and a batch-size histogram keyed by kv_hit
3) run 72h collection and assess if selector needs to consider recent kv_hit or batch-shape

maya: opening rollback ticket now and will execute immediate canary reduction. tagging @samir for dash work.

perf-bot: rollback executed for rollout 0x8b2c on accel-3 at 02:40 UTC; canary reduced to 0%.

maya: rollback complete. p95 trending down toward baseline within ~90s. keeping watch for 30m.

samir: I'll add dashboard panels: timeseries for kernel_launch_count (per-route), heatmap for memcpy_us, and a histogram widget for req_batch_size split by kv_hit. will include a small alert rule for launch_count/token ratio.

julie: follow-up items for postmortem: consider per-request kernel probing (cheap probe run) or selector heuristic that weighs recent kv_hit and batch-size distribution. record traces + flamegraphs in the ticket.

liam: agree. also evaluate whether we can amortize launch overhead with micro-batching for short runs or a lighter-weight kernel path.

maya: thanks everyone. attaching trace trace_20260108_0216_4410 and logs to the rollback ticket. :thumbsup:
